They are large canines with long, bushy tails that can be bred and [[Taming|tamed]]. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Wolf fang|0star=40%| 1star=2 (80%)| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf meat|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf pelt|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf trophy| 0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}}}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the daytime|limit=3|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=6|stars=Yes|frequency=5}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=4, within 10 meters|frequency=-|stars=Inherited from the parent}} {{spawn row|type=During "You are being hunted" [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=6|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Wolf Mountain]]|limit=8|frequency=4|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating wolves|Aggressive creature strategies#Wolf}} === Attack === This attack has three variations, each with its own 5-second cooldown: a left-swinging bite, a right-swinging bite, and a lunging bite (70 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). In practice, this means that Wolves will typically attack three times in a quick succession before retreating for a moment. These attacks extend 2 meters out in a 60.1-degree horizontal arc and can be used within 2 meters of a player. ==Taming== ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming|Taming.]]'' Wolves can make for powerful allies, both when following a player and when roaming around the built structures. Nighttime Wolves try to despawn during the day, so the taming of starred Wolves must be started during the night. Tamed Wolves will not retaliate against players when they or other Wolves are attacked/killed. A Wolf attacked by a player will be frightened, running around the nearby area for a few seconds before returning to their normal state. Once the taming has started, they will no longer try to flee and will also eat during the day. Taming a Wolf takes 30 minutes, if given enough food. == Breeding == Wolves can breed provided the Wolf is happy and well-fed with [[Boar Meat]] or other raw meat except wolf meat, seeker meat, and bear meat, and there is another Wolf within 3 meters, and no more than 4 Wolves within 10 meters. Once these requirements are met, the Wolf will accumulate love points with each other until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy will last a minimum of 1 minute, after which the birth of the baby Wolf is random chance. Once born, the baby Wolf will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. == Gallery == Wolf1.jpg Wolf2.jpg 1a.png|Comparison of 0, 1 and 2-star Wolves. ==Notes== *A wolf's size is affected by its star ranking. A 2-star Wolf is significantly larger than a 0-star Wolf. *Wolves can be transferred by boat by building a dock with a plank directly over the boat's deck. Wolves don't like to use staircases, so make it as flat as possible. Once the Wolf is over the boat, break the planks it is standing on to load the Wolf onto it. *Wolves will try to fight [[Serpent|Serpents]]. *Wolves will take collision damage if placed on top of the boat. Collision can occur from fish, rocks, and other unknown entities. The collision can occur at any time regardless of the boat's speed; and when it does, it will instantly kill the Wolf. This also occurs with Boars. *When roaming around an area where enemies drop meat, Wolves can not only sustain their numbers but multiply at an alarming rate. This has the advantage of keeping an area highly safe, though overpopulation can become a problem (running into players/carts, attacking structures, stutter on lower end systems, noise). *Tamed Wolves that are set to follow a player will remain where they are when the player logs out or portals beyond their detection range, regardless of the duration of the player's absence. Furthermore, tamed Wolves will resume following the player when they portal/log back in, without needing to manually set them to follow again. *Like (most/all?) creatures, Wolves have infinite stamina and will happily swim across an ocean if you sail slow enough for them to follow you. *Wolves can stand firm on steeper slopes than you can. You can use tame Wolves to your advantage when scaling steep cliffs, as you can lean on them while recovering stamina. However, in other circumstances, their eagerness to approach may nudge you into a tight corner or even off of a precipice. *When being raided by Wolves, it is not necessary to be near a structure for a raid to occur, unlike most raids. *2 Star Wolves can destroy stone structures == Lore == {{Quote|There are friends in Valheim but you must seek them amongst your enemies. Old friends, fire-kin, moon-singers. For centuries they have hunted alongside you, now you must remind them of the old covenant between your people and theirs. Flesh is their delight and must be your offering.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[fr:Loup]] [[cs:Vlk]] [[ru:Волк]] [[de:Wolf]]

They are slender, legless frost dragons with ice-blue scales and four horns. Drakes are the male offspring of their mother, [[Moder]]. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Drake trophy|0star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Freeze gland|0star=1}}|stars=0}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=Up to 3 [[spawn points]] in [[Drake Nest]] (100 meter altitude)|frequency=0|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the tall [[Mountain]]s (100 meter altitude)|limit=2|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=During "A cold wind blows from the mountains" [[Events|event]] before defeating [[Moder]]|limit=3|stars=No|frequency=6}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Drake Mountain]]|limit=4|frequency=8|stars=No}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Drakes|Aggressive creature strategies#Drake}} === Spit cold === Fires three balls of ice at the player, inflicting the [[Frost (effect)|Frost]] effect (90 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]] damage each). Each projectile travels at 15 meters per second for up to 10 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 10–20 degrees. This attack can be used within 5–15 meters of the player and has a 6-second cooldown. == Gallery == Two drakes vs 2 Vikings Valheim.jpg|Two Drakes attacking two Vikings as seen in Valheim PC Gamingshow 2020 Reveal Trailer[https://youtube.com/watch?v=oNx-9YsOpBo Valheim PC Gamingshow 2020 Reveal Trailer] A group of drakes around a ruined structure in Mountain Valheim.jpg|A group of Drakes around a ruined structure in Mountain as seen in the game's Microsoft Store and Xbox Announcement Trailer[[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vPEGKJlE9LE Valheim – Microsoft Store and Xbox Announcement Trailer]] Drake4.jpg|A Drake's frost ball attack ==Notes== *Originally introduced as a "Dragon Hatchling",[https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-745.0-750.0 https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-755.70-755.86] they were renamed to "Drakes" before release.https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-477.0-477.36 Drakes are still referred to in game files as a "Hatchling". *Drakes have a maximum chase distance of 200 meters from their spawn position. After that, they will drop aggro more easily. *Players are likely to find Drakes close to a [[Dragon Egg]] protecting it. *The drops from Drakes are unusually valuable. Their [[Freeze Gland]]s, glowing blue objects dropped on death, are necessary for all frost-based weapons and foods, and their trophy is used to make the helmet for [[Wolf Armor]]. *Appearance-wise, they greatly resemble an [[wikipedia:Amphiptere|Amphiptere]], a winged, legless type of dragon, in stark contrast to Moder who resembles a huge wyvern. *Drakes may be weak to fire, however, because of the massive damage difference between [[Fire Arrow]]s and [[Obsidian Arrow]]s, Obsidian are stronger (Fire totaling 44 and Obsidian totaling 52) **This does not make their fire weakness useless, as Fire arrows make a good replacement if you do not have Obsidian arrows yet or just to save materials. == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me be aware of the Frost wyrms, one of the most ancient kins sprung from Ymir's body. The most common form of the wyrm are the Drakes, the small males that cares for the offspring. Most often they can be seen poised by rocky nests guarding the eggs. In contrast, the females are much larger and a rare sight to behold, but once angered they provide a vicious foe.|[[Runestone]]}} ==References== {{Creatures}} [[fr:Drac]] [[ru:Дракон]] [[cs:Drak]]

Their appearance is distinctly werewolf-like, standing on two legs with a black fur coat. Unlike their [[Frost Caves|Frost cave]] [[Ulv|counterparts]], Fenrings only walk on their hind-legs. == Drops== {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Fenring trophy|0star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Wolf fang|0star=1}}|stars=0}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountain]]s during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=2|frequency=3|stars=No}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Fenrings|Aggressive creature strategies#Fenring}} === Claw === Swings their claw in a 3-meter 90-degree horizontal arc to scratch the player (85 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). This attack has a 3-second cooldown and can be used within 2.5 meters of the player. This also has a second variation where, despite the attack name, Fenrings lunge forward and bite the player; besides the animation, it's completely identicalAside from visuals, the animations also have very minor differences in their properties. The claw swing animation is 1.37 seconds long and hits after 0.65 seconds, while the bite animation is 1.53 seconds long and hits after 0.71 seconds. This is a hitbox time differential of 0.06 seconds; for reference, the parry window is 0.25 seconds. to the other variant and both share a single cooldown. === Jump === Pounces on the player and swings in with both claws (95 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). This hits in a 3-meter 90-degree horizontal arc. This attack can be used every 8 seconds when within 5–9 meters of a player, meaning it's disabled while standing close to Fenrings. == Gallery == Fenring sight.jpg Fenring03.png ==Notes== *The name "Fenring" is derived from [[wikipedia:Fenrir|Fenrir]], the same way [[Surtling|Surtlings]] derive from Surt. Fenrir (sometimes spelled Fenris or Fenrisulfr, "the Fenrir/Fenris-wolf") is a giant Wolf from Norse and Germanic mythology who will swallow the god Odin during Ragnarökr. He is the son of Loki. == Lore == {{Quote|Watch for him in moonlight Haunter of the night. Soft of foot Sharp of tooth Slow to stalk Quick to bite.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[ru:Фенринг]] [[fr:Fenring]]

The '''Standing green-burning iron torch''' is a light source that can be built using the [[Hammer]] within range of a [[Forge]]. It requires [[Guck]] as fuel.

The standing green-burning iron torch can hold up to six Guck at once. With 1/6 fuel, a standing green-burning iron torch will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. This attack has two variants, each with its own 3-second cooldown: a slash with his left claw and a slash with his right claw. He can use this attack when within 9 meters of a player. === Spin === Fader leans slightly on his right side before spinning to attack the surrounding area in a 8.5-meter radius circle around himself (140 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). He can use this ability every 20 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. === Flamebreath === Fader charges up and releases a 17-meter line of fire. It leaves lingering fire on the ground with a radius of 4 meters that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (60 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The flames last for 14 seconds. This attack cannot be blocked and can only be used every 25 seconds between 5–85% health when within 2–20 meters of a player. === Meteors === Fader rises on his hind legs and then stomps onto the ground calling forth 10 meteors, similar to [[Yagluth|Yagluth's]] meteor attack (40 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 120 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The meteors fall from the sky 60 meters behind Fader and 90 meters off of the ground in a 15-meter radius sphere. They fall at an initial velocity of 30 meters per second and can travel for up to 8 seconds before despawning. Upon impact, they leave green flames in a 5-meter radius circle that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (80 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 80 [[Damage types#Spirit|Spirit]], 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damageDue to what is presumably a typo or balancing change, this attack does not actually use the Fader_MeteorSmash_AOE prefab but instead uses the Fader_WallOfFire_AOE prefab. The MeteorSmash prefab does 300 Fire, 100 Spirit, 300 Tier 0 Chop and 300 Tier 0 Pickaxe damage but remains unused in any of Fader's properties.). These flames linger for 20 seconds. This attack can be used every 25 seconds while Fader is between 25–100% health. Under 25% health, it can be used every 18 seconds. He can use this ability while a player is within 30 meters. === Roar === When a player is within 100 meters, Fader can shoot eight glowing orbs out of his mouth into that air directly above him. These travel at an initial velocity of 20–50 meters per second for up to 20 seconds before despawning. They have a spread of 20–60 degrees. Upon impact, these orbs summon one [[Charred Warrior|Summoned Charred Warrior]] or [[Charred Marksman|Summoned Charred Marksman]] with a 50% chance of either. A maximum of seven of each creature can be summoned this way; since they have a unique ID from their regular counterparts, naturally-spawning Charred Warriors and Charred Marksmen do not count toward these spawn caps. Fader will still attempt to use ability even after reaching the spawn caps. These summoned enemies have 50 health and do half the damage of their regular counterparts. They also take friendly fire damage from Fader's attacks. This ability can be used every 45 seconds between 35–55% health, and every 26 seconds while under 35% health. === Wall of fire === Between 15–90% health, Fader can draw a line on the ground with his right paw which summons a wall of fire around the player that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Fire]], 80 [[Damage types#Spirit|Spirit]], 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This wall is is made up of 12 individual 4-meter radius circles of fire that appear 8 meters from the player, starting from the furthest point from Fader and moving clockwise with a delay of 0.25 seconds between each circle. These are generated relative to the player's current position, meaning that the player can create more room for themself to maneuver by continuously moving. This attack can be used every 60 seconds when within 40 meters of a player. Each circle is active for 20 seconds. === Notes === == Aftermath == === Creature spawning === Defeating Fader unlocks [[Charred Marksman|Charred Marksmen]] and [[Charred Warrior|Charred Warriors]] to spawn at night in the [[Meadows]], [[Black Forest]], [[Swamp]], [[Mountain]] and [[Plains]]. '''Frigid Kiln''' is a structure used to produce {{Item link|Liquid Frost}} out of {{Item link|Ice}}. Liquid Frost is the fuel of the [[Frost Foundry]].

==Availability==
* {{Item link|Frostcore}} can be obtained from [[Winding Tunnels]].
* {{Item link|Ice}} can be obtained by mining [[Ice Sheet]]s on the shore of the [[Deep North]], or dropped from [[Greydwarf (Deep North)|Greydwarfs]] in the Deep North

==Building==
The Frigid Kiln is found in the Crafting category of the [[Hammer]] and requires a nearby [[Workbench]] to build. It cannot be placed on wood, in water or on sloped surfaces. It costs:
* {{Item link|Stone|20}}
* {{Item link|Frostcore|10}}
* {{Item link|Ice|5}}

It has 1,500 durability. It is resistant to blunt, pierce, slash and chop damage, and immune to fire, frost, poison and spirit damage.

==Usage==
Ice is the kiln's only input; it is added like fuel, and no other item is needed. The kiln holds up to 25 [[Ice]] at a time. It produces one [[Liquid Frost]] every 30 seconds by consuming five Ice, so a full load of 25 Ice becomes five Liquid Frost in 150 seconds. Each Liquid Frost is ejected as soon as it is made.

Like the [[Smelter]], the Frigid Kiln stops working while its smoke is blocked.

'''Frost Foundry''' is a structure used to craft in the [[Deep North]]. It hardens [[Moulds|Casts]] into finished Deep North weapons, armor, shields, staffs and the {{Item link|Intricate Key}}.

==Building==
The Frost Foundry is found in the Crafting category of the [[Hammer]] and requires a nearby [[Workbench]] to build. It cannot be placed in water or on sloped surfaces. It costs:
* {{Item link|Iron|15}}
* {{Item link|Stone|20}}
* {{Item link|Frostcore|10}}

It has 500 durability. It is resistant to pierce and frost damage, weak to chop damage, and immune to poison and spirit damage.

==Usage==
It can be fueled with [[Liquid Frost]], which is made in the [[Frigid Kiln]]. It holds up to 20 Liquid Frost, and each unit lasts 10 seconds. Fuel is only used while an unfinished cast is inside.

A [[Moulds|Cast]] can be placed at the center to create the final item. The Frost Foundry holds one cast at a time. The process consumes five Liquid Frost and takes 50 seconds. Finished items cannot burn if left inside. Items made in the Frost Foundry come out at full durability.
